arxiv-2310-08243.title: Computing Twin-Width Parameterized by the Feedback Edge Number
arxiv-2310-08243.creator: Jakub Balabán, Robert Ganian, Mathis Rocton
arxiv-2310-08243.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jakub Balabán, Robert Ganian, Mathis Rocton. The problem of whether and how one can compute the twin-width of a graph—along with an accompanying contraction sequence—lies at the forefront of the area of algorithmic model theory. While significant effort has been aimed at obtaining a fixed-parameter approximation for the problem when parameterized by twin-width, here we approach the question from a different perspective and consider whether one can obtain (near-)optimal contraction sequences under a larger parameterization, notably the feedback edge number k k .

We especially would like to thank Michael Lechner and Franco Peracchi for feedback and suggestions. We are also g
arxiv-2403-03649.creator: Enzo Brox, Riccardo Di Francesco
arxiv-2403-03649.description: Abstract Many individuals hesitate to disclose their sexual orientation, anticipating that disclosure may alter how others respond to them. At the same time, concealing one’s identity can entail substantial personal and social costs. Understanding how others react to sexual orientation disclosure is therefore central to evaluating the broader consequences of coming out.

arxiv-2512-04229.title: 𝒁 ′ Z^{\prime} portal dark matter from post-inflationary reheating: WIMPs, FIMPs, and UFOs
arxiv-2512-04229.creator: and Keith A. Olive
arxiv-2512-04229.description: Abstract We investigate the production of dark matter (DM) via a heavy Z ′ Z^{\prime} mediator during the post-inflationary reheating epoch. In particular, we study production from three mechanisms which are smoothly connected to one another: WIMP-like freeze-out, FIMP-like freeze-in, and ultra-relativistic freeze-out (UFO). This is the first systematic study of Z ′ Z^{\prime} portal DM which includes UFO.

pmc-10684955.title: Hippocampal glial inflammatory markers are differentially altered in a novel mouse model of perimenopausal cerebral amyloid angiopathy
pmc-10684955.creator: Jimcy Platholi, Roberta Marongiu, Laibaik Park, Fangmin Yu, Garrett Sommer, Rena Weinberger, William Tower, Teresa A. Milner, Michael J. Glass
pmc-10684955.description: Dementia is often characterized by age-dependent cerebrovascular pathology, neuroinflammation, and cognitive deficits with notable sex differences in risk, disease onset, progression and severity. Women bear a disproportionate burden of dementia, and the onset of menopause (i.e., perimenopause) may be a critical period conferring increased susceptibility.

pmc-10745818.creator: Luka Morita, Shima Jalali, Abolfazl Vaheb, Rawan Elsersawy, Kunj Golwala, Asad Asad, Patricia I. Dolez, James D. Hogan, Mohammad Abu Hasan Khondoker, Dan Sameoto

pmc-11533711.title: ASPRONET: A facilitated online education project for radiation therapists in the Asia-Pacific region
pmc-11533711.creator: Craig Opie, Aidan Leong, Chetana Vartak, Iain Ward, Sandra Ndarukwa
pmc-11533711.description: In 2019, the International Atomic Energy Agency approved a technical co-operation project, aimed at supporting clinical decision making and continuing professional education of radiation oncologists, medical physicists and radiation therapists (RTs) in Low-and-Middle Income Countries (LMICs) in the Asia Pacific region. From this, the Asia-Pacific Radiation Oncology Network (ASPRONET) was formed in 2020.

pmc-11675903.title: Microgels of N-Isopropylacrylamide Copolymerized with an Amphiphilic Acid for the Delivery of Doxorubicin
pmc-11675903.creator: Teresa G Rodriguez-Tellez, Héctor Magaña, José M Cornejo-Bravo, Giovanni Palomino-Vizcaino, Kenia Palomino-Vizcaino, Gianluca Viscusi
pmc-11675903.description: This study aims to design microgels that are thermo- and pH-sensitive for controlled doxorubicin (Dox) release in response to tumor microenvironment changes. N-isopropylacrylamide (NIPAAm) is widely used for thermoresponsive tumor-targeted drug delivery systems for the release of therapeutic payloads in response to temperature changes.

pmc-12539372.title: Characterizing the Patient Experience of Idiopathic Subglottic Stenosis in Pregnancy
pmc-12539372.creator: Sarah Benyo, Radhika Duggal, Daniela Schmulevich, Justin Lau, Katherine Miller, Anastasia Christ, Laurence Gascon, Katherine Singh, Rebecca C Nelson, Paul C Bryson, Michael S Benninger, Robert R Lorenz, William S Tierney
pmc-12539372.description: ObjectiveTo characterize surgical interventions in pregnancy and postpartum periods and compare them to baseline periods (outside of pregnancy/postpartum) for patients with idiopathic subglottic stenosis (iSGS).MethodsA retrospective chart review was performed for patients undergoing endoscopic treatment for iSGS during pregnancy, postpartum, and baseline periods at The Cleveland Clinic between July 1, 2000 and January 1, 2025.

pmc-12542046.title: Dilemmas and strategies in the working experience of resident training nurses rotated in the intensive care unit: a qualitative study
pmc-12542046.creator: Ruike Zhang, Daxing Shao, Haifeng Huang, Yichun Zhang, Jing Lin, Wenping Wu, Haiyan Liang, Rongli Lian, Song Zhou
pmc-12542046.description: BackgroundIn high-pressure environments such as intensive care units (ICUs), newly graduated nurses often experience heightened transition shock during role adaptation, which increases the risk of burnout and turnover. Consequently, facilitating a smooth transition for nurses during their ICU rotations is a persistent challenge for nursing managers and educators.

pmc-12585887.title: Function of the tail in myliobatid rays: role in controlling body stability
pmc-12585887.creator: Júlia Chaumel, Connor White, George Lauder
pmc-12585887.description: Eagle rays, cownose rays and manta rays are the only batoid families exhibiting oscillatory locomotion, and are characterized by long, slender tails. This study investigates whether tail length influences body stability when the pectoral fins are held in an extended, static position.

pmc-12644571.title: Platelets regulate neural and oligodendroglial progenitors when infiltrating the brain parenchyma
pmc-12644571.creator: Christina Dimitriou, Maria Anesti, Stefanos Kaplanis, Theodora Mourtzi, Aggeliki Dimopoulou, Dimitrios Dimitrakopoulos, Filippos Katsaitis, Maria Nousia, Konstantina Mastori, Kyriaki Karassavidou, Efthimia Aleiferi, Dimitrios Lagogiannis, Esra Tahir, Amber R. Philp, Adamantia Kouvela, Constantinos S
pmc-12644571.description: The mammalian, including the human, postnatal brain harbors distinct neurogenic and oligodendrogenic progenitor populations, whose activity during homeostasis and degeneration is closely related to blood vessels. Here, we investigated the regulatory role of platelets, that are easily and unlimitedly accessible and can modulate tissue regeneration.

pmc-12984800.title: Augmented Prediction of N Parameter in Breast Cancer: Is It Possible with Shear-Wave Elastography Ultrasound Radiomics?
pmc-12984800.creator: Martina Caruso, Ludovica Rita La Rocca, Arnaldo Stanzione, Nicola Rocco, Tommaso Pellegrino, Daniela Russo, Maria Salatiello, Andrea de Giorgio, Roberta Pastore, Simone Maurea, Arturo Brunetti, Renato Cuocolo, Valeria Romeo
pmc-12984800.description: Simple SummaryUltrasound (US) is still the most sensitive modality to predict axillary lymph node (ALN) status in patients with breast cancer (BC) but suffers from a low and variable specificity. A Simple Logistic Machine Learning algorithm was used with US B-mode and SWE-derived radiomics features of 133 primary BC lesions to identify cases with positive ALN status.

pmc-13383598.title: Spectral Pattern of Chocolate Production: Early Detection of Quality Problems
pmc-13383598.creator: Yağmur Küçükduman, İkra Doğa Korkmaz, Hüseyin Güray Çiftçi, Gökhan İpkin, Sinem Argün, Zeynep Pınar Kara, Gonca Bilge Özel, Özge Taştan Ülkü, Ömer Said Toker, Zeynep Mutlu
pmc-13383598.description: Quality defects in chocolate can be classified as physicochemical quality problems and structural instability (blooming). Both problems can be detected after production and generally take time to become visible. Therefore, early detection tools are necessary to prevent economic losses in the food industry.

pmc-13533564.title: The dark genome in cardiovascular medicine
pmc-13533564.creator: Despoina Kesidou, Simon D Brown, Lars Maegdefessel, Igor Ulitsky, Andrew H Baker
pmc-13533564.description: Graphical Abstract Graphical AbstractThe dark genome landscape and therapeutic targeting in cardiovascular disease. Schematic overview of functional components within the dark genome. (Left) Non-coding RNAs, transposable elements, regulatory DNA regions (promoters, enhancers), introns and intergenic regions, pseudogenes and structural elements (telomeres, centromeres) modulate cardiovascular homeostasis.

pmc-13570024.title: Tear MicroRNA-Based Molecular Signature for Keratoconus Stratification: A Cross-Cohort Integration Study
pmc-13570024.creator: Shao-Hsuan Chang, Kuo-Hsuan Hung, Hsieh-Fu Tsai, Chung-Pei Ma, Hao-Chang Chiang, Lung-Kun Yeh
pmc-13570024.description: Keratoconus (KC) is a progressive corneal ectatic disorder characterized by structural remodeling and immune-associated molecular alterations. However, whether tear-derived microRNAs reflect corneal molecular changes remains unclear. We analyzed three publicly available corneal transcriptomic datasets (N = 112) to identify immune-associated gene expression patterns using differential expression analysis and Gene Set Enrichment Analysis.

uslaw-usc-t16-s430a3.title: 16 U.S.C. § 430a–3 — Applicability of laws and regulations to acquired lands and interests therein
uslaw-usc-t16-s430a3.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t16-s430a3.description: United States Code, Title 16 (Conservation); Chapter 1 (National Parks, Military Parks, Monuments, And Seashores); Subchapter LX (National Military Parks). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Lands and interests therein acquired pursuant to sections 430a–1 to 430a–3 of this title shall thereupon become a part of the Kings Mountain National Military Park and be subject to all the laws and regulations applicable thereto.
